en.title: AMR: national plans are expanding faster than the systems needed to measure and control resistance
en.deck: WHO’s 2026 country survey, WOAH’s 2024 animal-use baseline and ECDC’s 2025 clinical surveillance show that plans and reporting have expanded faster than financing, diagnostics and point-of-use measurement.
en.regime: Global AMR governance has broadened, but financing, reference laboratories and animal-use measurement remain incomplete.
en.key_risk: Plans remain unfunded and veterinary-use data continue to rely on sales/import records, preventing reliable evaluation of stewardship and resistance trends.

pt-BR.title: Resistência antimicrobiana: planos nacionais avançam mais rápido que a capacidade de medir e conter o problema
pt-BR.deck: A autoavaliação da OMS de 2026, a linha de base animal da WOAH para 2024 e a vigilância clínica do ECDC para 2025 mostram que planos e reportes avançaram mais rápido que financiamento, diagnóstico e medição no ponto de uso.
pt-BR.regime: A governança global da resistência antimicrobiana se ampliou, mas financiamento, laboratórios de referência e medição do uso animal continuam incompletos.
pt-BR.key_risk: Planos permanecem sem financiamento e os dados veterinários continuam dependendo de vendas e importações, impedindo avaliar com confiabilidade a gestão de antimicrobianos e as tendências de resistência.

signal_rationale.delta: New primary releases published 16–18 November 2026 combine a global implementation-capacity survey, WOAH’s 2024 animal-use baseline and ECDC/WHO’s 2025 invasive-isolate surveillance. This is a distinct measurement-and-financing update to the existing October livestock-AMR dossier, not a repeat of its general One Health framework.
signal_rationale.evidence: WHO TrACSS: 173/183 countries report plans but only 22% report funding plus full implementation and 36% reference-laboratory capacity; WOAH ANIMUSE: 119 participants cover 74% of food-animal biomass, but only five used farm records; ECDC: 21/43 countries show ≥50% 3GC resistance in K. pneumoniae, 21/38 show ≥50% carbapenem resistance in Acinetobacter, and EU/EEA carbapenem-resistant K. pneumoniae bloodstream incidence is 72% above 2019.
signal_rationale.scale_path: National financing and laboratory capacity determine whether action plans generate surveillance; veterinary point-of-use data determine whether animal-use targets can be measured; standardized human clinical surveillance enables trend monitoring and accountability.
signal_rationale.transmission: Underfunded diagnostics and incomplete animal-use records weaken stewardship and prevention; resistant infections increase treatment complexity and hospital costs, while poor veterinary measurement obscures agrifood-sector exposure and policy effectiveness.
signal_rationale.falsifier: A material rise in funded and evaluated national plans, reference-laboratory coverage, farm-record reporting and falling comparable resistant bloodstream-infection incidence would weaken the implementation-gap thesis.

key_constraints: TrACSS is a country self-assessment, not an independent audit of budgets or service quality.
ANIMUSE quantities are primarily derived from sales and import records; only five of 119 quantitative participants used farm records.
The ANIMUSE 2019–2024 and 2018–2024 trend estimates use different participant groups and periods.
ECDC data concern invasive human clinical isolates; they are not population-wide prevalence estimates.
Animal antimicrobial-use data and human resistance data are not linked at matched country, pathogen, exposure and time levels; no causal attribution is made.
Growth-promotion findings are participant reports (29 of 148; ten uncertain), not an estimate of global animal production share.

producer_checks.corpus_comparison: Existing 2026-10-12 livestock-AMR report is a broad governance baseline. This report is a focused update on new TrACSS 2026, ANIMUSE 2024 and ECDC 2025 releases, with point-of-use data and implementation finance as the distinct thesis.
producer_checks.novelty_decision: Substantive new primary-data delta; same registered editorial line and kind, new date-specific report, no arbitrary program or topic.
